subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pratt vs Warren Trusses
description: A 60-second lesson on Pratt vs Warren Trusses.

hook.text: Not all trusses look the same. The diagonal pattern changes everything.

buildup.text: A Pratt truss has diagonals sloping toward the center. They carry tension.

discovery.text: A Warren truss alternates diagonal direction — each triangle shares the work.

twist.text: Pratt trusses work best for heavy spans. Warren trusses suit lighter, even loads.

climax.text: Most highway bridges use Pratt trusses — steel diagonals in tension are efficient.

punchline.text: Same triangles, different angles, completely different strengths.

quiz.question: What direction do the diagonals slope in a Pratt truss?
options: Away from the center toward the supports
Vertically with no slope at all

details.summary: Pratt trusses have vertical members and diagonal members that slope toward the center, putting diagonals in tension and verticals in compression under gravity loads.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing the right truss configuration optimizes material use and construction efficiency. Pratt trusses are preferred for steel bridges because long tension diagonals use less material than compression members that must resist buckling.
takeaways: Pratt truss diagonals carry tension while verticals carry compression under gravity
Warren trusses eliminate verticals, using only equilateral triangular patterns
Member orientation determines whether they carry tension or compression

faq.question: Why is having diagonals in tension advantageous in a Pratt truss?
faq.answer: Tension members can be made from slender rods or light sections because they cannot buckle. Compression members must be stockier to resist buckling, requiring more material for the same force. Since diagonals are the longest web members, keeping them in tension saves significant material.

faq.question: When would an engineer choose a Warren truss over a Pratt truss?
faq.answer: Warren trusses have fewer members and simpler connections, reducing fabrication cost. They are efficient when loads are applied at the panel points along both top and bottom chords.
